'''Hans Joachim''' "'''John'''" '''Schellnhuber''' (born 7 June 1950)<ref>[http://www.pik-potsdam.de/john/] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090103134306/http://www.pik-potsdam.de/john/ |date=3 January 2009 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last=Mossman | first=Kaspar | title=Profile of Hans Joachim Schellnhuber | doi=10.1073/pnas.0800554105 | volume=105 | issue=6 | journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences | pages=1783–1785 | pmid=18256180 | pmc=2538840| bibcode=2008PNAS..105.1783M | year=2008 | doi-access=free }}</ref> is a German [[atmospheric physicist]], [[climatologist]] and founding director of the [[Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research]] (PIK) and former chair of the [[Wissenschaftlicher Beirat der Bundesregierung Globale Umweltveränderungen|German Advisory Council on Global Change]] (WBGU).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.wbgu.de/en/council-members/ |title=WBGU: WBGU Council Members 2013–2016 |publisher=Wbgu.de |access-date=28 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141221153030/http://www.wbgu.de/en/council-members/ |archive-date=21 December 2014 }}</ref> Since 1 December 2023, Schellnhuber is the Director General of [[IIASA]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://iiasa.ac.at/news/jul-2023/hans-joachim-john-schellnhuber-appointed-as-iiasa-director-general | title=Hans Joachim (John) Schellnhuber appointed as IIASA Director General }}</ref>

==Education==
Schellnhuber studied [[mathematics]] and [[physics]], obtaining a doctorate in theoretical physics from the [[University of Regensburg]] in 1980,<ref name=sust>{{Cite web|url=http://sustainabilityscience.org/content.html?contentid=388|title=Curriculum at Forum: Science and Innovation for Sustainable Development|access-date=11 October 2021|archive-date=27 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181127022456/http://sustainabilityscience.org/content.html?contentid=388}}</ref> followed in 1985 by [[Habilitation#Germany|habilitation]] (qualification for office) in theoretical physics at the [[University of Oldenburg]]. In 1981, he became a postdoctoral fellow at the Institute of Theoretical Physics (ITP) at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]], working across the corridor from its director [[Walter Kohn]], who became one of his academic supervisors.<ref name="pnas.org">{{cite journal|author=Kaspar Mossman |title=Profile of Hans Joachim Schellnhuber |doi=10.1073/pnas.0800554105 |volume=105 |issue=6 |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |pages=1783–1785 |pmid=18256180 |pmc=2538840|bibcode=2008PNAS..105.1783M |year=2008 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Career==
[[File:Hans Joachim Schellnhuber MSC 2019 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Schellnhuber during the [[Munich Security Conference|MSC]] 2019]]
Originally interested in solid state physics and quantum mechanics, Schellnhuber became drawn{{when|date=June 2016}} to complex systems and nonlinearity or [[chaos theory]].<ref name="pnas.org"/> 
As a full professor for theoretical physics and then{{when|date=June 2016}} director at the [[Institute for Chemistry and Biology of the Marine Environment]] at Oldenburg University, he was involved in analysing the structure of ocean currents.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.wbgu.de/en/council-members/2008-2012/prof-dr-hans-joachim-schellnhuber/ |title=WBGU: Prof. Dr. Hans Joachim Schellnhuber |publisher=Wbgu.de |access-date=28 December 2013 |archive-date=30 August 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110830074109/http://www.wbgu.de/en/council-members/2008-2012/prof-dr-hans-joachim-schellnhuber/ }}</ref>

In 1991, he was called upon to create the [[Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research]] (PIK). He became its director in 1993 – helping it grow to become one of the world's most renowned climate research institutes with more than 300 employees following an interdisciplinary approach.<ref name=portrait>{{cite web|url=http://www.pik-potsdam.de/institute/index_html |title=Portrait of the Institute – PIK Research Portal |publisher=Pik-potsdam.de |access-date=28 December 2013}}</ref>

As early as 1995 Schellnhuber proposed the 2&nbsp;°C guardrail for global warming which was adopted first by the German government and the European Union and then, following the Copenhagen accord in 2009, as a global target by governments worldwide.<ref>{{cite book|url=http://www.cambridge.org/de/knowledge/isbn/item1173798/?site_locale=de_DE |title=Avoiding Dangerous Climate Change: Climatology and climate change |publisher=Cambridge University Press |year=2006 |access-date=28 December 2013 |isbn=978-0-521-86471-8 |editor=Hans Joachim Schellnhuber|display-editors=etal}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Meinshausen | first1=Malte | last2=Meinshausen | first2=Nicolai | last3=Hare | first3=William | last4=Raper | first4=Sarah C. B. | last5=Frieler | first5=Katja | last6=Knutti | first6=Reto | last7=Frame | first7=David J. | last8=Allen | first8=Myles R. | title=Greenhouse-gas emission targets for limiting global warming to 2 °C | journal=Nature| volume=458| year=2009 | issue=7242 | issn=0028-0836 | doi=10.1038/nature08017 | pages=1158–1162| pmid=19407799 | bibcode=2009Natur.458.1158M | s2cid=4342402 }}</ref>

From 2001 to 2005 Schellnhuber served as research director of the [[Tyndall Centre]] in England and became a visiting professor at the [[University of Oxford]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ox.ac.uk/gazette/2005-6/weekly/241105/notc.htm#8Ref |title=Oxford University Gazette, 24 November 2005: Notices |publisher=Ox.ac.uk |access-date=28 December 2013 |archive-date=27 April 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130427220600/http://www.ox.ac.uk/gazette/2005-6/weekly/241105/notc.htm#8Ref }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.eci.ox.ac.uk/people/schellnhuberjohn.php |title=Environmental Change Institute (ECI) – Oxford University |publisher=Eci.ox.ac.uk |access-date=28 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131230232830/http://www.eci.ox.ac.uk/people/schellnhuberjohn.php |archive-date=30 December 2013 }}</ref>

Schellnhuber has been professor at the [[University of Potsdam]], Germany,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://puls.uni-potsdam.de/qisserver/rds;jsessionid=E9DDFD8D1F613F5861ECD755DA177562.node3?state=verpublish&status=init&vmfile=no&moduleCall=webInfo&publishConfFile=webInfoPerson&publishSubDir=personal&purge=y&personal.pid=1404&noDBAction=y&init=y |title=PULS – Potsdamer Universitätslehr- und Studienorganisationsportal – Prof. Dr. Hans-Joachim Schellnhuber |language=de |publisher=Puls.uni-potsdam.de |date=23 December 2013 |access-date=28 December 2013 |archive-date=14 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210614075845/https://puls.uni-potsdam.de/qisserver/rds;jsessionid=E9DDFD8D1F613F5861ECD755DA177562.node3?state=verpublish&status=init&vmfile=no&moduleCall=webInfo&publishConfFile=webInfoPerson&publishSubDir=personal&purge=y&personal.pid=1404&noDBAction=y&init=y }}</ref> and an external professor at the [[Santa Fe Institute]] in the US.<ref>{{cite web |author=Hans Joachim (John) Schellnhuber |url=http://www.santafe.edu/about/people/profile/Hans%20Joachim%20%28John%29%20Schellnhuber |title=Hans Joachim (John) Schellnhuber &#124; Santa Fe Institute |publisher=Santafe.edu |access-date=28 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131230231900/http://www.santafe.edu/about/people/profile/Hans%20Joachim%20%28John%29%20Schellnhuber |archive-date=30 December 2013 }}</ref>

As a long-standing member of the [[Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change]]<ref name=sust/> which was jointly awarded the [[2007 Nobel Peace Prize]], Schellnhuber has been a coordinating lead author of the synthesis chapter of Working Group II of the IPCC's [[Third Assessment Report]]. He has warned of dire consequences of continued [[global warming]]<ref name="ipsnews.net">{{cite news |url=http://www.ipsnews.net/news.asp?idnews=48791 |title=CLIMATE CHANGE: Four Degrees of Devastation |author=Stephen Leahy |publisher=IPS |date=9 October 2009 |access-date=28 December 2013 |location=UXBRIDGE, Canada |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120305064103/http://www.ipsnews.net/news.asp?idnews=48791 |archive-date=5 March 2012 }}</ref> As an expert<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Profile of Hans Joachim Schellnhuber|first=Kaspar|last=Mossman|date=12 February 2008|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|volume=105|issue=6|pages=1783–1785|doi=10.1073/pnas.0800554105|pmid=18256180|pmc=2538840|bibcode=2008PNAS..105.1783M|doi-access=free}}</ref> on [[Tipping point (climatology)|climatological tipping points]], he is a public speaker on the subject.<ref name="ipsnews.net"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://sciencewatch.com/dr/nhp/2009/09julnhp/09julnhpLentET/ |title=Timothy M. Lenton & Hans Joachim Schellnhuber |publisher=ScienceWatch.com |date=12 February 2008 |access-date=28 December 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news| url=http://dotearth.blogs.nytimes.com/2009/03/13/scientist-warming-could-cut-population-to-1-billion/ | work=The New York Times | title=Scientist: Warming Could Cut Population to 1 Billion | first=James | last=Kanter | date=13 March 2009 | access-date=4 May 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://beyondzeroemissions.org/media/radio/professor-schellnhuber-potsdam-institute-talks-pre-industrial-carbon-levels-safe-climate |title=Professor Schellnhuber of the Potsdam Institute talks pre industrial carbon levels for safe climate |publisher=Beyond Zero Emissions |access-date=28 December 2013 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120708082053/http://beyondzeroemissions.org/media/radio/professor-schellnhuber-potsdam-institute-talks-pre-industrial-carbon-levels-safe-climate |archive-date=8 July 2012 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.dw-world.de/dw/article/0,,3907790,00.html |title=German Scientist Warns Climate Change Accelerating &#124; Germany |publisher=Dw-world.de |date=29 December 2008 |access-date=28 December 2013}}</ref>

In 2017, Schellnhuber said that unless climate action is taken by 2020, the world "may be fatally wounded."<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.bbc.com/news/science-environment-48964736 |title = Twelve years to save Earth? Make that 18 months|work = BBC News|date = 24 July 2019|last1 = McGrath|first1 = Matt}}</ref>

==Achievements==
Schellnhuber has helped create numerous iconic concepts such as the analysis of [[tipping point (climatology)|tipping elements]] in the climate system,<ref name="pnas.org"/><ref>{{cite journal|author=Hans Joachim Schellnhuber |title=Tipping elements in the Earth System |doi=10.1073/pnas.0911106106 |pmid = 19995979|volume=106 |issue = 49|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |pages=20561–20563|pmc=2791592 |bibcode=2009PNAS..10620561S |year = 2009|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Kaspar Mossman |title=Tipping elements in the Earth's climate system |doi=10.1073/pnas.0705414105 |pmid = 18258748|volume=105 |issue = 6|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |pages=1786–1793|pmc=2538841 |bibcode=2008PNAS..105.1786L |year = 2008|doi-access=free }}</ref> the burning embers,<ref>{{cite journal|author=Timothy M. Lenton & Hans Joachim Schellnhuber |title=Tipping the scales |publisher=Nature |date=22 November 2007 |doi=10.1038/climate.2007.65 |journal=Nature Reports Climate Change |volume=1 |issue=712 |pages=97–98|doi-access=free |bibcode=2007NatCC...1...97L }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|url=http://www.pnas.org/content/early/2009/02/25/0812355106.full.pdf+html |title=Assessing dangerous climate change through an update of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) "reasons for concern" |date= March 2009|access-date=28 December 2013 |doi=10.1073/pnas.0812355106 |volume=106 |issue=11 |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |pages=4133–4137 |pmid=19251662 |pmc=2648893 | last1 = Smith | first1 = JB | last2 = Schneider | first2 = SH | last3 = Oppenheimer | first3 = M |display-authors=etal |bibcode=2009PNAS..106.4133S |doi-access=free }}</ref> and the budget approach for emissions.<ref>{{cite press release |url=http://www.wbgu.de/en/press-appointments/press-releases/2009-09-01-press-release/ |title=WBGU: 2009-09-01 Press Release |publisher=Wbgu.de |date=1 September 2009 |access-date=28 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131230232139/http://www.wbgu.de/en/press-appointments/press-releases/2009-09-01-press-release/ |archive-date=30 December 2013 }}</ref>

==Honors==
In 2002, Schellnhuber received the [[Royal Society]]'s Wolfson Research Merit Award<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.uea.ac.uk/mac/comm/media/press/2002/nov/New+UEA+professor+awarded+top+science+honour?mode=print |title=New UEA professor awarded top science honour |publisher=Uea.ac.uk |date=4 November 2002 |access-date=28 December 2013 |archive-date=31 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131231001758/http://www.uea.ac.uk/mac/comm/media/press/2002/nov/New+UEA+professor+awarded+top+science+honour?mode=print }}</ref>  
In 2004 Her Majesty [[Queen Elizabeth II]] appointed him to [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE).<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.pik-potsdam.de/news/archive/archive-2006/potsdam-climate-expert-hans-joachim-schellnhuber-becomes-chief-government-advisor-1 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120918062630/http://www.pik-potsdam.de/news/archive/archive-2006/potsdam-climate-expert-hans-joachim-schellnhuber-becomes-chief-government-advisor-1 |archive-date=18 September 2012 |title=Potsdam climate expert Hans Joachim Schellnhuber becomes Chief Government Advisor – PIK Research Portal |publisher=Pik-potsdam.de |date=1 December 2006 |access-date=28 December 2013 }}</ref>  
In 2005, the National Academy of Sciences (US) appointed him as a member.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nasonline.org/site/Dir/2049378569?pg=vprof&mbr=1006657&returl=http://www.nasonline.org/site/Dir/2049378569?pg=srch&view=basic&retmk=search_again_link |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120324091215/http://www.nasonline.org/site/Dir/2049378569?pg=vprof&mbr=1006657&returl=http:%2F%2Fwww.nasonline.org%2Fsite%2FDir%2F2049378569%3Fpg=srch&view=basic&retmk=search_again_link |url-status=dead |archive-date=24 March 2012 |title=National Academy of Sciences |publisher=Nasonline.org |access-date=28 December 2013}}</ref> He was awarded the [[Environment Prize (German Environment Foundation)|German Environment Prize]] in 2007. 
In that same year, he was elected a member of the [[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.leopoldina.org/en/members/list-of-members/list-of-members/member/Member/show/1221/|title=List of Members|website=www.leopoldina.org|language=en|access-date=22 April 2020|archive-date=14 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210614075843/https://www.leopoldina.org/en/members/list-of-members/list-of-members/member/Member/show/1221/}}</ref>

In 2011, he was the first German to receive the Volvo Environment Prize, which is the highest-ranking award in the field of environmental sciences worldwide.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.environment-prize.com/content/view/72/107 |title=Volvo Environment Prize – Laureate 2011 |publisher=Environment-prize.com |access-date=28 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131230234749/http://www.environment-prize.com/content/view/72/107 |archive-date=30 December 2013 }}</ref> He was honoured with the [[Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany]] (first class) as well<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.stk.brandenburg.de/sixcms/detail.php/bb1.c.264943.de |title=Bundesverdienstkreuz für Klimaforscher Hans Joachim Schellnhuber und das Vogelschützer-Ehepaar Litzbarski |publisher=Stk.brandenburg.de |access-date=28 December 2013 |language=de}}</ref> and holds honorary doctorates from Copenhagen University<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nat.ku.dk/nyheder/klimaforsker_doktor21112011/ |title=Nyheder – Københavns Universitet |publisher=Nat.ku.dk |access-date=28 December 2013 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130106130023/http://www.nat.ku.dk/nyheder/klimaforsker_doktor21112011/ |archive-date=6 January 2013 }}</ref> and [[Technische Universität Berlin]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pressestelle.tu-berlin.de/medieninformationen/2012/juni_2012/medieninformation_nr_1532012/ |title=Stabsstelle Presse, Öffentlichkeitsarbeit und Alumni: Medieninformation Nr. 153/2012 |publisher=Pressestelle.tu-berlin.de |access-date=28 December 2013 |language=de}}</ref>

The German magazine Cicero in 2012 ranked him amongst the 500 most important German intellectuals.<ref>{{cite web|date=2012|title=Cicero Ranking 2012 – Günter Grass und Alice Schwarzer spitze &#124; Cicero Online|url=http://www.cicero.de/berliner-republik/liste-der-500-guenter-grass-und-alice-schwarzer-spitze/52978|access-date=28 December 2013|publisher=Cicero|language=de}}</ref> In 2017, Schellnhuber was awarded the [[Blue Planet Prize]] of the Asahi Glass Foundation.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.af-info.or.jp/blog/b-info_en/2017-blue-planet-prize-commemorative-lectures.html |title=2017 Blue Planet Prize Commemorative Lectures |publisher=af-info.or.jp |access-date=9 August 2017}}</ref>

==Civic involvement and service==
As one of the leading climate scientists worldwide, he has been a consultant to the former President of the [[European Commission|European Union Commission]], [[José Manuel Barroso]].<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://europa.eu/rapid/pressReleasesAction.do?reference=IP/07/283&format=HTML&aged=0&language=EN&guiLanguage=en |title=Press release – World renowned experts to advise President Barroso on energy and climate change |publisher=Europa.eu |access-date=28 December 2013}}</ref> In 2007, he was appointed Chief Government Advisor on Climate and Related Issues during Germany's EU Council Presidency and G8 Presidency.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.g-8.de/nn_94680/Content/EN/Artikel/2006/12/2006-12-01-experten-beraten-beim-klimaschutz__en.html |title=G8 Summit 2007 Heiligendamm – Climate change experts to advise German government |publisher=G-8.de |access-date=28 December 2013}}</ref>

In 2007, Schellnhuber started "A Nobel Cause – Nobel Laureate Symposium Series on Global Sustainability" in Potsdam, bringing together Nobel Laureates from all disciplines with leading sustainability scientists.<ref>{{cite web|title=Welcome to the Nobel Cause Symposium Series – Nobel Cause Symposium|url=http://www.nobel-cause.de/|access-date=28 December 2013|publisher=Nobel-cause.de|archive-date=29 January 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120129195203/http://www.nobel-cause.de/}}</ref> In 2009, this event took place in London and in 2011 in Stockholm, where the UN secretary-general's High Level Panel on Sustainability came to the meeting to receive a [[Stockholm Memorandum|memorandum]] that was fed into the Rio+20 conference in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.un.org/en/sustainablefuture/pdf/World_leaders_urged_PR.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=28 June 2017 |archive-date=12 July 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120712211416/http://www.un.org/en/sustainablefuture/pdf/World_leaders_urged_PR.pdf }}</ref>

Schellnhuber offers scientific insights to business leaders, as a member of the Climate Change Advisory Board of [[Deutsche Bank]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.banking-on-green.com/en/content/acting_sustainably/climate_change_advisory_board_3183.html |title=Home – Deutsche Bank Responsibility |publisher=Banking-on-green.com |date=20 December 2013 |access-date=28 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110917063007/http://www.banking-on-green.com/en/content/acting_sustainably/climate_change_advisory_board_3183.html |archive-date=17 September 2011}}</ref> and chair of the governing board of the [[European Institute of Innovation and Technology]]'s Climate Knowledge and Innovation Communities (EIT Climate KIC).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://eit.europa.eu/newsroom-and-media/news-archive/single-view/article/climate-kic-office-in-the-eit-headquarters-inaugurated.html |title=European Institute of Innovation and Technology – Newsroom & Media |publisher=Eit.europa.eu |access-date=28 December 2013 }}{{Dead link|date=May 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>
In 2012, he was the lead-author of a report commissioned by the [[World Bank]]<ref name="sust" /> on possible impacts of a 4 degrees Celsius warming towards the end of the 21st century.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://climatechange.worldbank.org/content/climate-change-report-warns-dramatically-warmer-world-century |title=Climate Change Report Warns of Dramatically Warmer World This Century |publisher=Climatechange.worldbank.org |date=18 November 2012 |access-date=28 December 2013}}</ref> This report received a lot of attention worldwide.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2012/11/18/world-bank-climate-change-report_n_2156082.html |title=World Bank Climate Change Report Says 'Turn Down The Heat' On Warming Planet |publisher=Huffington Post |date=18 November 2012 |access-date=28 December 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://news.xinhuanet.com/english/sci/2012-11/19/c_131984227.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140105102247/http://news.xinhuanet.com/english/sci/2012-11/19/c_131984227.htm |archive-date=5 January 2014 |title=World Bank warns of climate change disaster – Xinhua &#124; English.news.cn |publisher=News.xinhuanet.com |date=19 November 2012 |access-date=28 December 2013}}</ref> That same year, Schellnhuber presented the keynote at the gala dinner that opened the high-level segment of the world climate summit [[COP18]] in Doha, Qatar.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.pik-potsdam.de/news/in-short/schellnhuber-gives-talk-to-high-ranking-representatives-of-states |title=Doha World Climate Summit: Schellnhuber gives talk to high-ranking representatives of states — PIK Research Portal |publisher=Pik-potsdam.de |access-date=28 December 2013 |archive-date=3 July 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130703061431/http://www.pik-potsdam.de/news/in-short/schellnhuber-gives-talk-to-high-ranking-representatives-of-states }}</ref> In the presence of UN Secretary-General [[Ban Ki-moon]] and [[UNFCCC]]'s boss [[Christiana Figueres]], a few days later Schellnhuber signed an agreement with the [[Qatar Foundation]] to jointly create a Climate change research institute in Qatar – a remarkable step as the country's wealth for decades had been based on exporting fossil fuels.<ref>{{cite news|last=Vidal |first=John |url=https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/poverty-matters/2012/dec/06/green-desert-doha-climate-talks?INTCMP=SRCH |title=Green thinking takes root in midst of desert in Doha climate talks &#124; John Vidal &#124; Global development |publisher=theguardian.com |date=6 December 2012 |access-date=28 December 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.gulf-times.com/qatar/178/details/334677/qatar-to-set-up-climate-centre |title=Qatar to set up climate centre |publisher=Gulf Times |date=6 December 2012 |access-date=28 December 2013}}</ref>

In 2013, Schellnhuber was one of 18 prominent international scientists to launch the Earth League, a global interdisciplinary alliance of leading research institutes that focus on Earth system analysis and sustainability science, including economy.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hzg.de/mw/earthleague/ |title=Miniweb Earth League Startseite |publisher=Hzg.de |date=7 February 2013 |access-date=28 December 2013}}</ref> UN Security Council members Pakistan and UK asked him to speak at a meeting of the Council under the [[Arria Formula]], the meeting at the UN headquarter in New York was attended by UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon.<ref>{{cite news|last=Krause |first=Flavia |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/2013-02-15/climate-change-s-links-to-conflict-draws-un-attention.html |title=Climate Change's Links to Conflict Draws UN Attention |publisher=Bloomberg |date=15 February 2013 |access-date=28 December 2013}}</ref> In the runup of the world climate summit in Warsaw, Schellnhuber discussed possible ways forward with the president of [[Cop19]], the Polish Minister of the Environment [[Marcin Korolec]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.genios.de/presse-archiv/artikel/ZEIT/20131107/-so-ein-totaler-quatsch/4D3CF13DD087432D25139D436FD9752C.html|title="So ein totaler Quatsch!"...|work=Die Zeit|date=11 July 2013|language=de|access-date=6 February 2014|archive-date=14 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210614075853/https://www.genios.de/presse-archiv/artikel/ZEIT/20131107/-so-ein-totaler-quatsch/4D3CF13DD087432D25139D436FD9752C.html}}</ref> To advance the state of science, Schellnhuber initiated{{when|date=June 2016}} the Inter-Sectoral Impact Model Intercomparison Project (ISI-MIP) that involves more than 30 research teams from 12 countries.<ref>{{cite press release |url=http://www.pik-potsdam.de/news/press-releases/recognizing-the-elephant-in-the-room-future-climate-impacts-across-sectors |title=Recognizing the Elephant in the Room: Future Climate Impacts across Sectors |publisher=PIK Research Portal |date=16 December 2013 }}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> In 2013, the scientific journal ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' called it the "first comprehensive global-impact project" – it aims at identifying robust insights as well as research gaps, based on a yet unprecedentedly broad comparison of computer simulations of future climate change impacts such as [[water scarcity]], floodings, or yield changes.<ref>{{cite journal| last1=Schiermeier |first1=Quirin| title=Water risk as world warms |journal=Nature|date=31 December 2013|volume=505|issue=7481|pages=10–11|doi=10.1038/505010a| pmid=24380936|bibcode=2014Natur.505...10S|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/earth-insight/2013/dec/17/planet-climate-change-risk-drought-famine-epidemic|title='Whole world' at risk from simultaneous droughts, famines, epidemics: scientists|author= Nafeez Ahmed|date=17 December 2013|work=theguardian.com }}</ref> In 2013, Schellnhuber's efforts resulted in the Impacts World Conference in Potsdam<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.climate-impacts-2013.org/index.php?article_id=1|title=Impacts World 2013 – International Conference on Climate Change Effects, Potsdam, 27–30 May|access-date=6 February 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140221234017/http://www.climate-impacts-2013.org/index.php?article_id=1|archive-date=21 February 2014}}</ref> followed by a special feature on first ISI-MIP results in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences ([[PNAS]]).

Schellnhuber has been serving as chair of the Climate-KIC (Knowledge and Innovation Community) governing board, which is affiliated to the [[European Institute of Innovation and Technology]] (EIT).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.climate-kic.org/about/how-we-are-organised/governing-board/|title=Governing Board :John Schellnhuber, Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research|publisher=Climate-KIC|access-date=6 February 2014|archive-date=22 February 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222195931/http://www.climate-kic.org/about/how-we-are-organised/governing-board/}}</ref> This institution aims at fostering low-carbon entrepreneurship and innovation.

Schellnhuber signed the 2005 [[Potsdam Denkschrift]] calling for a change in thinking to enable [[sustainable development]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.vdw-ev.de/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=15&Itemid=9&lang=en|title=Potsdam Denkschrift - Potsdam Manifesto 2005|date=17 July 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110717134702/http://www.vdw-ev.de/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=15&Itemid=9&lang=en|access-date=11 October 2021|archive-date=17 July 2011}}</ref>

==Personal life==
He is married to Margret Boysen, who is the author of ''[[Alice, the Zeta Cat and Climate Change]]''.<ref>{{Cite news |last=unfccc.com |title=Explaining Climate Science with a Climate Fairy Tale“Alice, the Zeta Cat and Climate Change”#Art4Climate |url=http://newsroom.unfccc.int/unfccc-newsroom/explaining-climate-science-with-a-climate-fairy-tale/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201044507/http://newsroom.unfccc.int/unfccc-newsroom/explaining-climate-science-with-a-climate-fairy-tale/ |archive-date=2017-12-01 |access-date=2026-07-11 |work=UNFCCC |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pik-potsdam.de/members/boysen/cv |title=Curriculum Vitae – PIK Research Portal |publisher=Pik-potsdam.de |access-date=28 December 2013}}</ref>
